title: Trapping Rain Water
keyIdea: Water above bar i = min(tallest on its left, tallest on its right) − height[i]. Two pointers: always process the lower side; if height[left] ≤ height[right], the right has a wall at least that tall, so left's water depends only on leftMax (and vice versa). O(n), O(1).

approaches.name: Prefix and suffix max arrays
approaches.idea: leftMax[i] and rightMax[i] = tallest bar at/left of i and at/right of i; water += min of the two − height[i].
approaches.why: Three linear passes and two arrays of size n.

approaches.name: Two pointers with leftMax / rightMax
approaches.idea: Move the lower side inward; update its max, or add max − height as water.
approaches.why: Each step settles one bar; only four integer variables.

options: min(tallest left, tallest right) − its height (if positive)
the gap to the next bar

quiz.q: Why can the lower side be settled with only its own max?
options: The other side is at least as tall, so it isn't the limiting wall
The other side is always shorter
